prompt: A 30-day backfill contains 180 runs with 12 tasks each. Each task averages 20 minutes and consumes one pool slot. The shared bottleneck has 80 effective slots; live workflows require 48 at peak and policy reserves 20 percent of total capacity as headroom. Backfill demand also adds 60 metadata-database connections, while the database safe ceiling is 120 and live use is 90. The current model service receives 1,500 requests/s. One instance is safe at 120 requests/s at the target utilization; a zone failure removes 40 percent of instances. Candidate offline F1 rises from 0.86 to 0.89, but the evaluation population excludes the newest region, online/offline features disagree on 7 percent of paired rows, and no tested previous deployment revision is retained. Produce a correctness-first operating, capacity, promotion, security, privacy, cost and recovery plan with calculations.
directAnswer: Do not admit the full backfill or promote the model. First preserve current runs, pool/database signals, experiment/evaluation, feature samples, model/artifact/alias/deployment and user-impact evidence. Backfill contains 180 x 12 = 2,160 task executions and 2,160 x 20 = 43,200 task-minutes = 720 task-hours. Headroom is 20 percent of 80 = 16 slots. Compute spare by slots as 80 - 48 - 16 = 16 slots, giving an ideal slot-bound drain of 720 / 16 = 45 hours before failures, skew and overhead. But the database is tighter: only 120 - 90 = 30 safe connections remain, while proposed backfill needs 60. If each concurrent task consumes one connection, database capacity reduces reviewed backfill concurrency to at most 30 before extra database headroom; a safer policy reserves database margin and may reduce it further. Use a separate pool/queue, bounded max-active runs, waves, pause thresholds and exact interval/code/data identities. For serving, steady-state instances are ceil(1,500 / 120) = 13. To survive a 40 percent loss without exceeding the safe rate, planned total must satisfy 0.6N x 120 >= 1,500, so N >= 20.833 and at least 21 instances, subject to integer-zone distribution, feature/dependency capacity, cold start and tested load. Do not promote: the F1 comparison is not representative of the newest region, 7 percent feature mismatch violates parity, and rollback is not real without a retained compatible revision. Contain by keeping the current verified model, fix and test one feature definition with point-in-time/freshness semantics, evaluate on the required region and critical slices with absolute/relative thresholds and mature labels, retain and test immutable rollback, then use a bounded canary or side-effect-free shadow. Enforce separate author/operator/approver identities, least-privilege task/model/notebook access, immutable artifact digest/signature, audited alias/deployment changes, protected prediction/feature sampling, complete copy/retention policy and no sensitive values in telemetry. Track cost per successful interval, failed/retried task, training/evaluation, model revision and thousand predictions; include idle recovery capacity and backfill opportunity cost. Validate live SLO protection, exact outputs, model/feature request identity, serving under zone-loss load, rollback and teardown.
foundation: Capacity is constrained by the tightest shared dependency, not worker slots. Promotion requires representative evaluation, feature parity and reversible deployment. Better aggregate offline metrics cannot compensate for missing population coverage or an unsafe serving path.
reasoningSteps: Stop unbounded backfill and candidate promotion.
Calculate 2,160 tasks, 720 task-hours and 16 slot-spare capacity.
Design isolated bounded waves at the tighter constraint.
Calculate 13 steady instances and at least 21 for 40-percent loss.
Build immutable tested rollback and progressive delivery.
Apply security privacy audit and copy-retention controls.
Measure user recovery, correctness, capacity and unit cost.
seniorAnswer: The backfill is 720 task-hours. Slot policy leaves 16 slots, so ideal drain is 45 hours, but the database allows only 30 connections before any additional margin and is therefore an independent tighter guard against the proposed 60. I isolate and wave the work while protecting live SLOs. Serving needs 13 instances normally and at least 21 planned to retain 1,500 requests/s after losing 40 percent, before dependency and placement validation. I reject promotion despite higher F1 because the population excludes a region, paired features differ by 7 percent and rollback is unproved. I repair those contracts, retain an immutable prior revision, and canary only after gates pass.
weakAnswer: Use all 80 slots so 2,160 tasks finish quickly, scale to 13 model instances, and promote because F1 improved by three points. Retrain if the new region complains.
whyWeak: It starves live work, exceeds database connection capacity, lacks zone-loss capacity, treats a non-representative aggregate metric as a gate, ignores feature skew and has no rollback.

followUps.prompt: If average duration becomes 30 minutes, what is the ideal 16-slot drain?
followUps.answer: 2,160 x 30 = 64,800 task-minutes = 1,080 task-hours; 1,080 / 16 = 67.5 hours before overhead.

followUps.prompt: If the zone loss becomes 50 percent, how many instances are required?
followUps.answer: 0.5N x 120 >= 1,500, so N >= 25; placement and dependency capacity still require testing.

followUps.prompt: Can shadow traffic solve the region gap?
followUps.answer: It can compare candidate outputs on eligible live inputs without serving them, but it does not provide mature labels immediately and must be isolated from side effects, privacy leakage and capacity harm.

Recovery capacity supports the availability objective. Compare reserved, warm, cold-start and degradation designs using tested recovery time and business cost rather than eliminating headroom blindly.
